name: Garnet Brown
lede: Garnet Brown is a dark, reddish brown named for the gem rather than its namesake's usual red, close enough to our library's Ox-Blood Red to be a near-duplicate.

sections.title: A gem name turned brown
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas gives this swatch at plate I, hue 3, tone k, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system files it in block 16, a dark red [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates the same name to 1905, at plate 6, L 9 [1]. [[gem:garnet|garnet]] stones usually read as a deep brownish red, so the brown here leans the name's gem a shade further from pure red than the stone itself [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[morocco-red]], [[dusty-maroon]] and [[oxheart]], at 2.8, 4.1 and 4.2 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this reddish brown in 785 of 23,781 paintings, close to three and a half per cent, one of the more common colors in this group [2]. It peaks in the 1400s, in 73 of 945 paintings, at four times the overall baseline rate [2]. The earliest match is a Maya mural fragment from around the year 500, well over a thousand years before Ridgway named the color, so that is a lookalike hue, not evidence of garnet pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings and murals, and a match says nothing about the materials actually used [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
